title: Sparsity and granularity inequality
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f$ be a function from the $n$-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb F_2$ to the signs. If the spectral sparsity $s$ of the real-valued function obtained from $f$ is greater than $1$, then $s$ times the square of the spectral sparsity granularity at $s$ is at most $1$.
hypotheses_covered: spectral sparsity of the real-valued version of $f$ is strictly greater than $1$
